steps.t: Mix the chicken with curd, half the ginger and garlic, chili powder, turmeric and salt. Marinate.
Heat oil in a wide pan and sear the chicken in batches until lightly browned, about 6 to 8 minutes. Set aside.
Blend the tomatoes to a smooth puree.
Melt the butter in the same pan. Add the remaining ginger and garlic for 30 seconds, then the tomato puree. Cook until the oil separates.
Add the chicken and any juices, with a splash of water. Cover and simmer until cooked through.
Stir in the cream, garam masala and a pinch of sugar. Simmer 2 minutes, taste for salt, and serve with naan or rice.
Fry the sliced onions in oil until deep golden. Lift out onto paper and let them crisp.
Marinate the chicken with curd, ginger, garlic, chilies, spices, salt, half the fried onions, mint and coriander.
Boil plenty of salted water and cook the soaked rice until 70 percent done. Drain.
In a heavy pot, cook the marinated chicken with the tomatoes until the masala thickens.
Spread the rice over the chicken. Top with remaining fried onions, mint, coriander and ghee.
Seal the pot with foil and a tight lid. Cook on the lowest heat (dum).
Rest, covered, then fluff gently from the edges and serve with raita.
Blanch the spinach in boiling water, then dunk in cold water. Blend with green chilies to a smooth puree.
Shallow fry the paneer cubes until golden on the sides. Set aside.
Heat oil, add cumin, then the onion. Cook until golden.
Add ginger, garlic and tomatoes. Cook until soft and mushy.
Pour in the spinach puree with garam masala and salt. Simmer.
Add the paneer and cream. Simmer 2 minutes and serve hot with roti.

ing.q: 2 cups cooked (or 1 cup dried, soaked overnight)

steps.t: If using dried chickpeas, pressure cook them with salt until soft. Otherwise drain the cooked chickpeas.
Heat oil, add cumin, then onions. Cook until deep golden brown.
Add ginger, garlic and green chili. Stir for a minute.
Add the tomato puree and all the powdered spices. Cook until the oil separates.
Add the chickpeas and a cup of water. Simmer, mashing a few chickpeas to thicken the gravy.
Finish with lemon juice and coriander leaves. Serve with rice, bhature or roti.
Cook the dal with turmeric, salt and 3 cups water in a pressure cooker until completely soft. Whisk until creamy.
In a pan, heat a little oil and cook onion, tomato and green chili until soft.
Add the cooked mixture to the dal and simmer, adjusting water for the thickness you like.
For the tadka, heat ghee or oil until hot. Add cumin, sliced garlic and chili powder. Let the garlic turn golden.
Pour the sizzling tadka over the dal, garnish with coriander and serve with rice.
Heat oil, add cumin, then onion and ginger. Cook until golden.
Add tomatoes and the powdered spices. Cook until soft and the oil separates.
Add potatoes and cauliflower with salt and green chili. Mix to coat in the masala.
Cover and cook on low heat, stirring now and then, until the vegetables are tender. Sprinkle water only if sticking.
Finish with garam masala and coriander leaves.

ing.q: 1 cup basmati, rinsed and soaked 15 min

steps.t: Heat ghee or oil in a pot. Add the cumin and let it crackle.
Add the drained rice and gently stir for a minute.
Pour in 1.75 cups water and add salt. Bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce to the lowest heat and cook until the water is absorbed.
Switch off, rest covered, then fluff with a fork.
Hard boil the eggs, cool them in water, peel, and make a few light slits in each.
Heat oil and cook onions until golden brown.
Add ginger, garlic and green chili, then the tomatoes and powdered spices. Cook until the oil separates.
Add 1 cup water and salt. Simmer to a gravy.
Add the eggs, simmer 5 more minutes, and finish with garam masala and coriander.
Rinse the poha in a colander until soft but not mushy. Mix in salt, sugar and turmeric. Let it rest.
Heat oil. Fry the peanuts until crisp and set aside.
In the same oil add mustard seeds, curry leaves and green chili. When they splutter, add the onion (and potato if using).
Add the poha and peanuts. Toss gently and heat through.
Finish with lemon juice and coriander leaves.
Dry roast the semolina until fragrant and lightly colored. Set aside.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds, curry leaves, green chili and ginger.
Add onion (and carrot if using) and cook until soft.
Add 2.5 cups hot water and salt. Bring to a rolling boil.
Lower the heat and pour in the semolina in a stream while stirring to avoid lumps. Cover and cook.
Finish with lemon juice and serve hot.
Make the filling. Heat oil, add mustard seeds, curry leaves, green chili and ginger.
Add the onions and turmeric. Cook until soft.
Add the roughly mashed boiled potatoes, salt and a splash of water. Mix well and keep warm.
Heat a flat tawa until a drop of water sizzles. Pour a ladle of batter and spread thin in circles.
Drizzle oil around the edges and cook until the underside is crisp and golden.
Place filling in the center, fold the dosa and serve with chutney and sambar.

ing.q: 1 cup dried kidney beans, soaked overnight

steps.t: Pressure cook the soaked rajma with salt and enough water until very soft.
Heat oil, add cumin, then onions. Cook until golden.
Add ginger, garlic and green chili, then the tomato puree and powdered spices. Cook until the oil separates.
Add the cooked rajma with its liquid. Mash a few beans against the pot.
Simmer until the gravy is thick and rich.
Garnish with coriander and serve with steamed rice.
Knead the flour with water, a pinch of salt and a little oil into a soft dough. Rest it.
Mix the mashed potato with green chili, coriander, cumin, chili powder, garam masala and salt.
Roll a dough ball into a small disc, place a spoon of filling in the center and seal the edges.
Gently roll it flat, dusting with flour as needed.
Cook on a hot tawa, brushing oil on both sides, until golden spots appear.
Serve hot with curd, pickle or butter.
Wash the rice and dal together and soak briefly.
In a pressure cooker, heat ghee and add cumin, ginger and green chili.
Add vegetables if using, then the rice and dal. Stir with turmeric and salt.
Add 4 cups water, close the lid and cook until soft and porridge-like.
Mash lightly, top with a spoon of ghee, and serve with curd or pickle.
Pressure cook the dal with turmeric and water until soft. Mash it.
Boil the vegetables in tamarind water with salt until tender.
Add the mashed dal and sambar powder. Simmer.
Temper: heat oil, add mustard seeds and curry leaves. Pour over the sambar.
Garnish with coriander and serve with idli, dosa or rice.
Boil tomatoes with tamarind water, turmeric and salt until the tomatoes break down.
Coarsely crush pepper, cumin and garlic together, then add to the pot.
Add 2 cups water and simmer gently. Do not boil hard.
Temper with oil, mustard seeds and curry leaves. Pour in.
Finish with coriander and serve as a soup or with rice.
Heat ghee, add cumin, then onion, ginger, garlic and chilies. Cook until golden.
Add carrots and peas with garam masala. Stir for 2 minutes.
Add the drained rice and gently toss.
Pour in 2.25 cups hot water and salt. Bring to a boil.
Cover and cook on the lowest heat until the water is absorbed.
Rest 5 minutes, fluff, and serve with raita.
Heat oil and fry the okra on medium-high heat without covering, until no longer sticky.
Remove the okra. In the same pan, add cumin and onions. Cook until golden.
Add tomato and the spices. Cook until soft.
Return the okra and toss gently. Cook uncovered for a few minutes.
Finish with a squeeze of lemon and serve with roti.
Heat oil, add cumin, then onion, ginger and green chili. Cook until soft.
Add tomato and capsicum if using, with turmeric and chili powder. Cook until mushy.
Add the crumbled paneer and salt. Mix well.
Sprinkle garam masala and coriander. Serve with roti or in a sandwich.
Mash the warm rice slightly with the back of a spoon.
Mix in curd, milk and salt until creamy.
Heat oil and add mustard seeds, green chili, ginger and curry leaves. Let them splutter.
Pour the tempering over the rice and mix. Garnish with coriander and serve.
Heat oil and fry the peanuts until golden.
Add mustard seeds, green chili and curry leaves. Let them splutter.
Add turmeric, then the rice and salt. Toss gently on low heat.
Turn off the heat, squeeze in lemon juice and mix. Serve.
Heat oil, add cumin, then onions. Cook until golden.
Add ginger and garlic, then the tomato puree and spices. Cook until the oil separates.
Add potatoes, peas, salt and 1.5 cups water.
Cover and simmer until the potatoes are tender.
Finish with garam masala and coriander. Serve with roti or rice.
Rub the brinjal with oil, prick it and roast directly over a flame or in a hot oven, turning until the skin chars and the flesh is soft.
Cool, peel off the skin and mash the flesh.
Heat oil, add cumin, garlic, ginger and green chili. Add onions and cook until golden.
Add tomatoes, turmeric and chili powder. Cook until soft.
Add the mashed brinjal and salt. Cook, stirring, until well blended.
Garnish with coriander and serve with roti.

ing.q: 3 tbsp, plus more for the pav

steps.t: Boil potato, cauliflower, peas and carrot with salt until very soft. Drain and mash roughly.
Melt butter in a wide pan. Add ginger, garlic and onions. Cook until golden.
Add capsicum and tomatoes. Cook until completely broken down.
Add chili powder, turmeric and pav bhaji masala, then the mashed vegetables with a cup of water. Mash firmly as it cooks.
Toast the pav in butter on a pan until golden.
Top the bhaji with butter, lemon and coriander. Serve with pav and raw onion.
Heat oil and cook the onions until deep golden brown.
Add ginger, garlic and green chili. Cook for a minute.
Add tomatoes and all powdered spices. Cook until the oil separates.
Add the chicken (and curd, if using) and salt. Sear, stirring, until it changes color.
Add 1 cup water, cover and simmer until the chicken is tender.
Finish with garam masala and coriander. Serve with rice or roti.

ing.q: 1 cup grated or 1 cup coconut milk

steps.t: Grind the coconut with ginger, garlic and a little water to a smooth paste (skip if using coconut milk).
Heat oil, add mustard seeds and curry leaves. Add onions and cook until soft.
Add tomatoes and the powdered spices. Cook until soft.
Stir in the coconut paste or milk, tamarind water, salt and a cup of water. Simmer.
Slide in the fish. Simmer gently without stirring too much until just cooked.
Rest 10 minutes for the flavors to settle, then serve with rice.
Beat the eggs with salt, turmeric and chili powder.
Stir in the onion, tomato, green chili and coriander.
Heat oil in a non-stick pan and pour in the mixture. Spread evenly.
Flip once and cook the other side until set.
Serve with toast or pav.
Whisk curd, besan, turmeric, salt and 3 cups water until completely smooth.
Pour into a pot and bring to a boil, stirring constantly so it doesn't curdle.
Lower the heat and simmer, stirring often, until it thickens and loses the raw besan smell.
Heat oil for the tadka. Add cumin, mustard seeds, curry leaves, green chili, ginger and chili powder. Pour over the kadhi.
Garnish with coriander and serve with rice.
Whisk besan with about 3/4 cup water, salt and the spices into a smooth, pourable batter. Rest briefly.
Fold in the onion, tomato, green chili and coriander.
Heat and lightly oil a non-stick pan. Pour a ladle of batter and spread thin.
Cook until the edges lift and the underside is golden. Flip and cook the other side.
Serve hot with green chutney or ketchup.
